subject: Finova - Decision criteria clarification: latency / cost / deployment / SLA
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@finova.com>
Cc: Ethan Moore <ethan.moore@finova.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Finova - Post-call recap & clarification on decision criteria

Hi Priya / Ethan

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a couple of clarifying questions so we can align the next steps with the right stakeholders on your side. I attached a short post-call recap and our Dedicated SLA brief for reference.

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use: real-time customer support assistant for high-value accounts (multi-turn chat with context).
- Peak QPS: expected ~150 concurrent sessions initially, with spikes to ~300 during peak business hours.
- Latency target: under 300ms p95 for single-turn responses; sub-500ms for multi-turn scenarios (including retrieval).
- Cost sensitivity: targeting cost/unit improvements vs current vendor; procurement will need an estimated TCO for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployments.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 + customer-managed KMS required; procurement will own the questionnaire.

Clarifying questions for your decision criteria (so we can prepare the right options):
1) Can you confirm the strict p95 latency SLO the business requires for the primary flows? Is 300ms p95 an absolute requirement or a stretch target?
2) For deployment mode, do you have a preference today (Hosted API for speed to market, Dedicated for predictable capacity, or Private for VPC/on-prem)? If undecided, who on your side is the economic buyer that will sign off on the budget/commitment?
3) Procurement process: who will manage the vendor eval and the timeline for completing the security questionnaires / procurement sign-off? Any known gating items (e.g., SOC2 attestation date, PoP requirements)?

Proposed next steps:
- Marcus (me) to send a concise Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private TCO + performance summary by EOD tomorrow.
- Ava to map technical stakeholder checklist and recommended config options for your expected QPS.
- If helpful, we can set a 30-min session with our SRE lead to walk your infra team through latency tuning and KV caching approaches.

Can you confirm the decision owners and whether procurement has an official RFP timeline?

Thanks
Marcus
Marcus Lin | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

Thanks Marcus
appreciate the recap. A few answers inline.

On 14 Feb 2028, at 09:15, Marcus Lin wrote:
> 1) Can you confirm the strict p95 latency SLO the business requires for the primary flows? Is 300ms p95 an absolute requirement or a stretch target?

300ms p95 is the target for single-turn responses
this is a hard requirement for our premium tier. For multi-turn we can tolerate up to 600ms p95 but we'd prefer <500ms if achievable.

> 2) For deployment mode, do you have a preference today (Hosted API for speed to market, Dedicated for predictable capacity, or Private for VPC/on-prem)? If undecided, who on your side is the economic buyer that will sign off on the budget/commitment?

We are leaning toward Dedicated (reserved capacity) for predictable performance and data isolation. Economic buyer will be our Head of Product, Anjali Rao (anjali.rao@finova.com). Procurement will still need cost breakdowns to recommend a commit level.

> 3) Procurement process: who will manage the vendor eval and the timeline for completing the security questionnaires / procurement sign-off? Any known gating items (e.g., SOC2 attestation date, PoP requirements)?

Procurement (procurement@finova.com) will manage the vendor eval. They need SOC2 Type II and a clear audit log / data retention policy. We expect procurement to complete vendor selection within 4–6 weeks, assuming no major security gaps.


Next steps for us: we'll loop in Anjali and the procurement contact. Please send the TCOs and SLA summary.

Priya
Priya Sharma
Senior Product Manager, Finova
priya@finova.com

Subject: Re: Finova - Post-call recap & clarification on decision criteria

Priya
thanks for the quick clarifications and for identifying Anjali as the economic buyer. That helps.

Posting the interim answers here and attaching a short TCO summary: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
high-level comparison:
- Hosted (fastest onboarding): minimal commit, pay-as-you-go; higher per-token cost; transparent latency but subject to multi-tenant noisy neighbors (we have mitigation policies). Good for PoC.
- Dedicated (recommended for you): reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, isolated tenancy, and configurable autoscaling; significantly lower per-token unit cost at commit levels. Supports the p95 latency target with the right capacity profile and tuning.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): maximum data isolation, customer-managed networking; higher ops overhead and longer onboarding. Best if procurement/legal require full control of network and keys.

SLA notes (from attached brief):
- Dedicated SLA: 99.9% uptime, p95 latency SLO configurable per-route; compensation clauses based on downtime minutes.
- Hosted SLA: 99.5% uptime standard for paid tiers; latency best-effort with burst protection.

Action items I committed to:
- Send TCO + perf summary by EOD (attached: 1 page).
- Set up technical sync with our SRE & Solutions Engineering
suggest Thu 16 Feb, 10:00am PT.

Ava
can you prepare the capacity sizing for 150–300 concurrent sessions and include expected p95 latency at each commit tier?

Thanks
Marcus

Hi Priya / team

Following up with the capacity and latency estimates Marcus requested. High-level guidance below; I'll send a short spreadsheet with the committed tiers and estimated monthly costs.

Capacity sizing (initial):
- 150 concurrent sessions baseline -> Recommended Dedicated pool: 4 x A100-equivalent nodes with continuous batching and KV caching. Expected p95: ~220–280ms for single-turn; ~350–450ms for multi-turn (with retrieval).
- 300 concurrent sessions baseline -> 8 x A100-equivalent nodes; expected p95: ~280–320ms single-turn with aggressive batching; ~420–520ms multi-turn.

Notes on cost:
- At a 12-month commit at the 4-node tier, approximate monthly cost is $XX,XXX (detailed spreadsheet to follow). Dedicated commit reduces per-token unit cost by ~40% vs Hosted at similar throughput.
- If procurement needs an on-prem/private option, we can provide a rough install & support estimate but that typically adds 20–30% overhead for setup and support.

SLA confirmation: Dedicated can be configured with a p95 latency SLO and 99.9% uptime. We will include trace-level logs and an audit log export (S3) to meet SOC2 evidence requests.

Next steps:
- I'll send the spreadsheet with the tiered costs and estimated performance by EOD today.
- Marcus to confirm meeting time for deep-dive (SRE + procurement invite).
- Priya to introduce Anjali + procurement contact so we can onboard them on the timeline.
